headline: CBIC amends Rule 20 of CGST Rules on cancellation of registration, effective 1 Dec 2026
reference: Notification No. 08/2026-Central Tax dated 25 November 2026 (CGST Second Amendment Rules, 2026)
summary_points: CBIC notifies the Central Goods and Services Tax (Second Amendment) Rules, 2026, amending Rule 20 of the CGST Rules, 2017.
New sub-rule (5): if returns are filed in time and all dues paid, registration is cancelled electronically by the common portal from the date sought, communicated in FORM GST REG-38.
New sub-rule (6): if returns or CMP-08 statements are not furnished or dues remain unpaid, the application goes to the proper officer for examination.
The amendment comes into force on 1 December 2026.
who_is_affected: Registered taxpayers applying for voluntary cancellation of GST registration, including composition taxpayers, and tax officers handling such applications.
action_required: Before applying for cancellation on or after 1 December 2026, file all required returns and CMP-08 statements and clear all tax, interest, fee and penalty dues to enable automatic cancellation.

social.linkedin:
CBIC has notified a change to Rule 20 of the CGST Rules, 2017, which governs cancellation of registration on the taxpayer's application.

Notification No. 08/2026-Central Tax, dated 25 November 2026, comes into force on 1 December 2026.

What changes:

- Where the cancellation application is filed, the required returns are furnished within the specified time and all tax, interest, fee or penalty is paid, the common portal will cancel the registration electronically from the date sought. This will be communicated in FORM GST REG-38.

- Where returns or CMP-08 statements (where applicable) are not furnished, or dues remain unpaid, the application will be forwarded to the proper officer for examination.

Practical takeaway: clean compliance before applying can mean a system-driven cancellation without officer intervention. Businesses planning to exit GST registration should review their return and payment status first.

Please verify the details with the official CBIC notification before acting.
